resultJson.description:
Slice 3 of 4 of #8, designed in docs/adr/0001-adr-start-spotify-from-spotify-refresh-token-fall.md. Today the first Spotify call with no session always goes to `initialAuth`, the browser sign-in, so `SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN` is never used at startup. This slice adds `SpotifyClient.signIn` and makes the `None` branch of `getOrRefresh` call it.

When `creds.configuredRefreshToken` is set, `signIn` posts one `grant_type=refresh_token` named "Refresh Token Exchange". The outcomes:
- Success: the lights start without a sign-in URL.
- 400 `invalid_grant` (`SpotifyTokenError.Rejected`): one WARN that contains no token, then a fall back to `initialAuth`.
- Any other failure fails that poll and leaves the session at `None`: `Failed` (429, 401 invalid_client, 5xx), transport errors, or `SpotifyTlsFailure("Refresh Token Exchange")`. The next poll tries the swap again, and no URL is logged.
- With no token, or a blank one, `signIn` goes straight to the browser sign-in.

Slices 1 and 2 have already landed: `SpotifyTokenError` (an enum), `SignInCodes` (once/make), `SpotifyCredentials.refreshToken: Option[String]` with `configuredRefreshToken`, the optional `refresh-token` in application.conf, `refreshWith`, and the retryable browser attempt. So this slice is a small change to `SpotifyClient` plus tests and docs. The sp_dc cookie and the `GET /authorize` request stay until slice 4: fakes must still answer `GET /authorize`, and the docs keep their sp_dc lines. The startup swap and the invalid_grant fallback ship together in one task. Splitting them would leave a state in which a revoked token fails every poll and never offers the browser.

Departures from the ADR, and notes on test evidence, each to be stated in the PR:
- (a) `refreshToken` is `Option[String]` and `SpotifyTokenError` is an enum. Both were already changed by the scala-fp review in #27.
- (b) `initialAuth` raises when the code exchange sends no refresh token, instead of storing "". That is already merged.
- (c) The rejected-token WARN carries `client_id` as log4cats context (MDC) next to the status. The client id is not a secret, since it already appears in the logged authorize URL. sbt runs suites in parallel in one JVM, and the WARN text has nothing specific to a test in it, so the context is what lets a test count "exactly one WARN" for its own client. `testkit.Tls.capturedLogs` therefore captures MDC when each event is appended.
- (d) AC 1 (token absent or blank) can't be shown by a test that fails on master. Master never sends a refresh_token grant at startup and always logs 'Please visit', so these rows pass there. They guard against a `signIn` that would send "" or "   ". The engine-level absent and rejected cases are the same: they pass on master. Every other AC has a test that fails on master.

tasks.title: signIn: start from the configured refresh token, falling back to the browser on invalid_grant
tasks.description:
Production changes, all in src/main/scala/client/SpotifyClient.scala:
- Add `def signIn: F[String]`, using the ADR's scaladoc.
- Change `getOrRefresh` to `case None => signIn`.
- `signIn` with `creds.configuredRefreshToken` None runs `initialAuth`.
- With Some(token), it runs `refreshWith("Refresh Token Exchange", token)` followed by INFO `Signed in to Spotify with the configured refresh token`. Apply `.recoverWith { case SpotifyTokenError.Rejected(_, status, _) => … }` to that exchange only. The handler logs WARN `Spotify rejected the configured refresh token (status: $status); signing in through the browser instead` through `logger.warn(Map("client_id" -> creds.clientId))(msg)`, then runs `initialAuth`. Never log the token, the body or `creds`. Every other error propagates.
- In `initialAuth`, add INFO `Signed in to Spotify through the browser` right after `session.set`, as ADR Observability requires.
- Leave `renew` unchanged.

Testkit: in src/test/scala/testkit/Tls.scala, `capturedLogs` must keep MDC. Logback 1.5's LoggingEvent reads MDC lazily, so subclass ListAppender in place and call `e.prepareForDeferredProcessing()` in `append` before `super.append(e)`.

Migrate existing tests:
- SpotifyClientSpec: 'signs in on first use…' and 'sign-in fails…' switch to `SpotifyCredentials("id", "secret")`. The first would otherwise swap and never reach authorization_code. The second would still pass, but for the wrong reason: it would fail before the code exchange.
- SpotifyTlsSpec: `spotify(...)` is called from `untrusted`, from `trusted`, and directly in 'the code exchange fails…'. Thread a creds parameter through both helpers, with no configured token by default, so 'the code exchange fails…' and 'signing in over a trusted certificate…' still reach Code Exchange and authorization_code. The fake answers any POST /api/token with 200, so a configured token would swap successfully. Only the renamed 'signing in against an untrusted certificate…' test passes `Some("refresh")` and asserts `assertNames(r, "Refresh Token Exchange")`.
- SpotifyTlsEngineSpec: in the third test, assert `Spotify Refresh Token Exchange failed` and rename it so it no longer says 'authorize call'.

New SpotifyClientSpec tests. Run every row under `TestControl.executeEmbed`: on master the valid and failed rows block forever in `initialAuth` waiting for a code, and under TestControl that fails straight away as non-termination instead of hitting munit's timeout. The setup:
- A recording fake built with `Client.fromHttpApp`. It records each POST /api/token form (grant_type, refresh_token, code) and each GET /authorize, and answers GET /authorize with Ok.
- The fake answers the refresh_token grant by token value. The row's configured token gets the row's answer. `refresh-9` gets `renewedTo("renewed", None)`.
- authorization_code gets `renewedTo("signed-in", Some("refresh-9"))`, and /v1/me/player goes through `playerFor`.
- Each row has its own client_id and a unique token value. Logs are captured with `(Tls.capturedLogs, Tls.loggingAt("client.SpotifyClient", Level.INFO)).tupled` and filtered on logger `client.SpotifyClient` plus the client_id: in the URL for 'Please visit', in MDC `client_id` for WARN.
- The browser path uses `SignInCodes.make[IO]`: start the poll, `IO.sleep`, hand the code via `SpotifyClient.callbackRoutes(codes).orNotFound.run(Request(GET, uri"/callback?code=…"))`, then join.

Rows:
- Valid, 200: the first poll plays, after exactly one refresh_token grant carrying the token. There is no authorization_code grant, no /authorize, and no 'Please visit' for that client_id. Fails on master: it hangs waiting for a code.
- 400 `{"error":"invalid_grant"}`: exactly one WARN for that client_id saying the configured refresh token was rejected. No captured event contains the token value; check every event's formatted message, MDC values and throwable messages. 'Please visit' is logged, and after the code is handed the poll plays. Fails on master: there is no WARN and no refresh_token grant.
- 429, 401 `{"error":"invalid_client"}`, 503: the poll fails with `SpotifyTokenError.Failed("Refresh Token Exchange", status, _)`. The session stays None, no 'Please visit' is logged for that client_id, and no authorization_code is sent. A second poll records a second refresh_token grant. Fails on master: it hangs at the code wait.
- None, Some(""), Some("   "): no refresh_token grant, 'Please visit' logged, and handing a code gives a playing poll. These rows pass on master; see the description's departure (d).
- AC5: the configured token is rejected and the browser sign-in returns refresh-9. Then call the public `spotify.renew` directly. The recorded token requests are exactly [refresh_token(configured), authorization_code, refresh_token(refresh-9)]. Fails on master, where the first entry is missing.

Run `sbt fix`, then `sbt check`.

tasks.title: Engine-level proof: lights follow playback when starting from a valid, rejected or absent token
tasks.description:
In src/test/scala/SyncEngineRunSpec.scala, add tests under `TestControl.executeEmbed` that run the whole engine starting with session `None`. Leave the existing `engine` helper and its tests alone: it hardcodes `Some(SpotifySession("token", "refresh"))` and a Deferred. Add a separate helper that builds:
- `SignInCodes.make[IO]`.
- A fake whose POST /api/token answers the refresh_token grant per case (200 or 400 `{"error":"invalid_grant"}`) and answers authorization_code with 200 and a refresh token.
- GET /authorize answering Ok (still requested until slice 4).
- /v1/me/player playing.
- A client built with `SpotifyCredentials(<unique client id per case>, "secret", token)`.

Cases:
- Valid token: frames are non-resting (playing) from shortly after the first poll at about 1.1 s, with no code handed. Fails on master, where the lights stay resting while sign-in waits for a browser code.
- Rejected token and absent token: frames stay resting until a code is handed via `SpotifyClient.callbackRoutes(codes).orNotFound.run(Request(GET, uri"/callback?code=code-1"))` at about 1.5 s simulated time, after the 1 s poll has opened the attempt. Run it alongside `e.run`, as the existing `alongside` and area tests do. After that, frames show the palette (non-resting). These two cases also pass on master, and the PR says so (departure (d)).

Use the suite's `isResting`/`playingFrames`. Run `sbt fix` and `sbt check`.

tasks.title: Docs: SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN is optional; how-it-works §1 describes the startup swap; DocsSpec
tasks.description:
README.md line 23: make the `SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN` row start with 'Optional.'. Say that the app starts from it without a browser sign-in, and signs in through the browser when it is empty or Spotify rejects it. Leave the SPOTIFY_SP_DC row alone; slice 4 removes it.

In docs/how-it-works.md §1 (lines 5–28), add the startup swap to the mermaid sequence diagram and the bullets:
- With SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN set, the first call posts `grant_type=refresh_token` and needs no browser.
- invalid_grant logs a WARN and falls back to the authorize URL.
- 429, invalid_client and 5xx fail that poll, and the next poll tries again.
- After a browser sign-in, the session keeps the refresh token Spotify sends with it.

Keep the existing sp_dc lines for slice 4. `.env.example` already has `SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN=` blank, so it needs no change.

Add src/test/scala/DocsSpec.scala: a munit FunSuite in the default package, like SyncEngineRunSpec, since DirectoryAndPackageName is enforced. Write a single test. It reads `README.md` with `java.nio.file.Files.readString(Paths.get("README.md"))`; tests aren't forked, so the working directory is the project root. It finds the line starting with "| `SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN` |" and asserts that the line exists and contains 'Optional'. The test fails against the current README. Run `sbt fix` and `sbt check`.

resultJson.brief:
Project: Scala 3 (3.9), Typelevel stack: Cats Effect 3.6, fs2, http4s 0.23 Ember, circe, pureconfig, and log4cats-slf4j over logback 1.5. sbt root project at `.`, with test sources in src/test/scala. `sbt fix` applies the Scalafix rewrites and formatting. `sbt check` lints, runs the tests with coverage, and fails below 90% statements / 85% branches overall or 70% statements in any file. Never lower these minimums or disable rules. Use brace syntax, given/using, and typed errors raised in F. Comment only what the code can't say. Test names say what they check, with no explanatory comments. Never print `.env`, `SpotifyCredentials` or `AppConfig`, and never log a token.

STATE: slices 1 and 2 of ADR docs/adr/0001-… are merged. Read the ADR's Decision, Failure modes, Observability and Slices 3 and 4. Already in place:
- src/main/scala/domain/spotify/SpotifyCredentials.scala: `case class SpotifyCredentials(clientId: String, clientSecret: String, refreshToken: Option[String] = None)` with `def configuredRefreshToken: Option[String]` (trimmed, None when blank). The ADR said `String = \"\"`; the scala-fp review changed it to an Option.
- src/main/scala/client/SpotifyTokenError.scala: `enum SpotifyTokenError extends RuntimeException { case Rejected(call: String, status: Status, body: String); case Failed(call, status, body) }`. `SpotifyTokenError.of(call, status, body)` gives Rejected only for 400 with JSON `error == \"invalid_grant\"`. getMessage carries the call, status and body, never the token.
- src/main/scala/client/SignInCodes.scala: `trait SignInCodes[F] { def attempt: F[F[String]]; def hand(code: String): F[Boolean] }`. `SignInCodes.make[F: Concurrent]` keeps one pending attempt, and a hand spends it. `SignInCodes.once(deferred)` wraps a Deferred as a single attempt.
- src/main/scala/client/SpotifyClient.scala: class `SpotifyClient[F[_]: Async: Network](client, creds, session: Ref[F, Option[SpotifySession]], codes: SignInCodes[F])`, plus an auxiliary constructor that takes `Deferred[F, String]`. Members:
  - `naming(call)(fa)` wraps SSL failures as `SpotifyTlsFailure(call, cause)`, with message `Spotify $call failed on its certificate: …`.
  - `initialAuth` (:66-101): `codes.attempt`, then `logger.info(s\"Please visit: $authUrl\")` (the URL contains `client_id=<id>`), then GET /authorize with the sp_dc Cookie ('Authorize'; removed in slice 4), then `waitForCode`, which blocks forever until a code is handed, then a POST of authorization_code ('Code Exchange'; on error it logs `Spotify Exchange Failed. Body:` and raises a RuntimeException). It raises if there is no refresh_token, otherwise `session.set(Some(SpotifySession(access, refresh)))`.
  - `getOrRefresh` (:106-109): `case None => initialAuth`. This is the line to change.
  - `renew` (:115, public): session Some means `refreshWith(\"Renew\", s.refreshToken)`; None falls back to the configured token or initialAuth. Keep as is. It logs `Renewed the Spotify access token`.
  - `private def refreshWith(call: String, refresh: String): F[String]` (:128-139) POSTs grant_type=refresh_token with Basic client creds, raises `SpotifyTokenError.of(call, status, body)` on a non-2xx answer, and on success sets `SpotifySession(access, resp.refresh_token.getOrElse(refresh))`. The session is untouched on failure.
  - `authorised(call, req)(read)`: `getOrRefresh`, send; on 401, `renew` and resend once.
  - `getPlaybackState` ('Playback Poll'), `getTempo` ('Tempo Lookup').
  - Companion object: `callbackRoutes[F](codes: SignInCodes[F])` (GET /callback?code=…, which calls `codes.hand` and answers Ok \"Success! Return to your terminal.\"), `serverResource(codes)`, and `resource(client, creds)`, which builds `SignInCodes.make`.
  - `private val logger = Slf4jLogger.getLogger[F]`. The logger name is `client.SpotifyClient`. For log4cats context use `logger.warn(Map(\"k\" -> \"v\"))(msg)`; Slf4jLogger puts the map into MDC.
- src/main/scala/SyncEngine.scala:115-119: the poller calls `spotify.getPlaybackState` every `pollingIntervalMs`, and on error logs ERROR `Spotify Poll Failed: $err` and treats it as nothing playing. So a failed sign-in poll is retried on the next tick with no extra code.
- src/main/resources/application.conf: `refresh-token = ${?SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN}`. Already optional.

TESTS / TESTKIT:
- src/test/scala/testkit/Tls.scala: `Tls.capturedLogs: Resource[IO, ListAppender[ILoggingEvent]]` attaches to the root logger. `Tls.logged(appender): List[ILoggingEvent]`. `Tls.loggingAt(name, Level)` temporarily sets a logger level. logback-test.xml sets root to WARN, so INFO lines ('Please visit', the 'Signed in…' lines) need `Tls.loggingAt(\"client.SpotifyClient\", Level.INFO)`. sbt runs suites in parallel in one JVM, so filter events by logger name AND a client_id unique to the test: 'Please visit' carries it in the URL, and the WARN carries it in MDC `client_id`. LoggingEvent reads MDC lazily, so the appender must call `prepareForDeferredProcessing()` at append time.
- TestControl: a program that waits forever (for example a sign-in nobody hands a code to) fails right away under `TestControl.executeEmbed` with a non-termination error. Outside TestControl it only hits munit's timeout. Put sign-in tests under TestControl.
- src/test/scala/client/SpotifyClientSpec.scala (CatsEffectSuite). Helpers:
  - `playing` JSON, `rejected` (401), `renewedTo(access, refresh: Option[String])`, `signedInBearer` (Bearer \"signed-in\"), `playerFor(req)` (playing only for signedInBearer, with no reject-once state).
  - `retryAfterFailedExchange` is the template for browser sign-in under TestControl: `SignInCodes.make[IO]`, `spotify.getPlaybackState.start`, `IO.sleep(1.second)`, `SpotifyClient.callbackRoutes[IO](codes).orNotFound.run(Request(Method.GET, uri\"/callback?code=…\"))`, `joinWithNever`. Fakes read the form with `req.as[UrlForm]` and `form.getFirstOrElse(\"grant_type\", \"\")`.
  - Fakes should answer GET /authorize (e.g. `Ok(\"login\")`) until slice 4. A 404 would also be ignored, because the body is only drained.
- src/test/scala/client/SpotifyTlsSpec.scala: a real TLS fake via `Tls.server(app)`, which returns `(port, IO[List[Request]])`. `fake()` answers any POST /api/token with 200. `spotify(client, session, code)` hardcodes `SpotifyCredentials(\"id\", \"secret\", Some(\"refresh\"))` and is called from `untrusted` (:53), from `trusted` (:58) and directly at :105, so a creds parameter has to go through both helpers. `assertNames(result, call)` checks the `SpotifyTlsFailure` call name.
- src/test/scala/SpotifyTlsEngineSpec.scala: the third test asserts `Spotify Authorize failed`. With the token configured, it becomes `Spotify Refresh Token Exchange failed`, because the SyncEngine ERROR line carries the SpotifyTlsFailure message.
- src/test/scala/SyncEngineRunSpec.scala: default package, `TestControl.executeEmbed`. `engine(setup, calls)` builds a fake Spotify with session Some, polling at 1000 ms. Helpers: `run`, `alongside(setup, duration)((engine, live) => …)`, `isResting`, `playingFrames` (t > 1.1 s). `SyncEngine.make[IO](config, live, spotify, zone, lights, Random, audio)`.
- SpotifyRenewSpec and SignInCodesSpec are unaffected (session Some).
- Test lint (.scalafix.test.conf): DirectoryAndPackageName (a file's package must match its directory; the root test dir means the default package), FileNameConsistent, no nulls or isInstanceOf, OptionContains, FilterSize (prefer `count`), and others. Running IO directly in tests is allowed.

DOCS: README.md:19-28 holds the env table. Row 23 is `| `SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN` | Refresh token for your Spotify account |`, and row 24 is SPOTIFY_SP_DC (keep it until slice 4). docs/how-it-works.md §1 is lines 5-28: a mermaid sequence diagram plus bullets, with sp_dc on lines 16 and 25 (keep them). Tests are not forked (`Test / fork` is unset until slice 4), so `Paths.get(\"README.md\")` resolves from the project root, as DocImages relies on.

The ADR's log wording, to use exactly: INFO `Signed in to Spotify with the configured refresh token`; WARN `Spotify rejected the configured refresh token (status: <status>); signing in through the browser instead`; INFO `Please visit: <url>` (unchanged); INFO `Signed in to Spotify through the browser`.
